intro: Many real objects are combinations of basic solids, like a capsule (cylinder with two hemispheres) or a toy top (cone on a hemisphere). To find the surface area, add only the surfaces you can see; to find the volume, add the volumes of the parts.
keyPoints: Surface area of a combination = sum of the curved/visible surfaces only.
Volume of a combination = sum of the volumes of the parts.
Slant height of a cone: l = √(r² + h²).
formulas: Cuboid: TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl), V = lbh
Cylinder: CSA = 2πrh, TSA = 2πr(r + h), V = πr²h
Cone: CSA = πrl, TSA = πr(l + r), V = (1/3)πr²h

examples.title: Cone on a hemisphere
examples.problem: A toy is a cone of radius 3.5 cm mounted on a hemisphere of the same radius. The total height of the toy is 15.5 cm. Find its total surface area. (π = 22/7)

examples.title: Joining two cubes
examples.problem: Two cubes, each of volume 64 cm³, are joined end to end. Find the surface area of the resulting cuboid.

examples.title: Volume of a cylinder
examples.problem: Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. (π = 22/7)
